section.title: WARNING: RISK OF REYE SYNDROME IN CHILDREN AND TEENAGERS

text.paragraph: Children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chickenpox or flu-like symptoms should not use this medicine. When using this medicine, if changes in behavior with nausea and vomiting occur, consult a doctor because these symptoms could be an early sign of Reye syndrome, a rare but serious illness.

Aspirin is indicated to reduce the risk of death and myocardial infarction in patients with acute coronary syndromes (unstable angina, non-ST elevation myocardial infarction, and ST elevation myocardial infarction) and suspected acute coronary syndromes.
Aspirin is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), active pathological bleeding, severe thrombocytopenia, or hemorrhagic diathesis.

Gastrointestinal adverse events including ulceration, bleeding, and perforation can occur at any time without warning symptoms. Caution is advised when co-administered with anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents.

Co-administration of aspirin with systemic NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen) may competitively inhibit platelet COX-1, attenuating aspirin cardioprotection. Concurrent use with heparin, warfarin, or direct oral anticoagulants substantially increases major bleeding risk.
